title: Decision: Event coalescing via try_recv drain without sleeping
description:
In kithd events.rs (lines 232-286), rapid-fire StateChange events are coalesced:
  1. Receive first event (blocking await)
  2. Drain all immediately available events via try_recv() without sleeping
  3. Emit one merged SSE frame

Comment at line 219-227 explains the rationale:
  Store writes are synchronous, so all StateChange events emitted by a single JMAP method call (e.g. Peer/deliver touching Contact + Chat + Message) are queued before any async yield. After the first recv().await unblocks, try_recv() captures all of them without sleeping, producing one merged SSE frame instead of three.

This is correct because:
1. JMAP method execution is synchronous (single-threaded Phase 1)
2. All state changes from one method land in the broadcast buffer before any async yield
3. try_recv() is non-blocking, so no sleep needed
4. Produces RFC 8620 §7.3 compliant merged state object
5. Test coverage confirms multi-type coalescing (line 1266+)

This is a non-obvious but correct optimization of the SSE output shape.
